abstention.statement: NXPH3 and CCDC136 do not share the complement-mediated synaptic pruning mechanism that links the rest of this gene set to schizophrenia. The GWAS Catalog reports no significant variants associated with schizophrenia for either gene. Furthermore, Open Targets lacks an association for CCDC136 and scores NXPH3 at 0.00, while protein interaction networks show no edges connecting these two genes to the C1QA/C4A/CX3CR1 complement cluster.
abstention.what_would_change_this: New genome-wide association studies demonstrating a robust genetic link between these genes and schizophrenia, or biochemical evidence showing they physically interact with or regulate the classical complement pathway in microglia or at synapses.

falsification.description: Knock out CSMD1 in human iPSC-derived neuron-microglia co-cultures and measure whether C4A/C4B-mediated synaptic pruning is significantly increased compared to wild-type controls.

hypotheses.mechanism: Structural variations in the complement genes C4A and C4B increase their expression and predispose individuals to schizophrenia by driving excessive classical complement cascade activation at synapses. CSMD1 encodes a complement inhibitor that localizes to synapses to protect them from inappropriate tagging by C4A. When CSMD1 is deficient or overwhelmed, the complement system excessively tags synapses, resulting in aberrant synaptic pruning by microglia and contributing to schizophrenia pathogenesis.
hypotheses.title: Loss of CSMD1 inhibition exacerbates C4A/C4B-mediated synaptic pruning in schizophrenia

falsification.description: Pharmacologically inhibit CX3CR1 in a human microglial model exposed to C1QA-opsonized synapses, and measure whether microglial activation and subsequent synapse engulfment are exacerbated.

hypotheses.mechanism: C1QA initiates the classical complement cascade, tagging synapses and prompting microglial cell activation for their elimination. CX3CR1, expressed on microglia, provides an inhibitory tone via the CX3CL1-CX3CR1 axis that regulates microglial reactivity and maintains neuroimmune homeostasis. Disruption of CX3CR1 signaling removes this brake, allowing C1QA-driven microglial activation to proceed unchecked and resulting in the excessive synaptic pruning characteristic of schizophrenia.
hypotheses.title: CX3CR1 dysregulation amplifies C1QA-initiated microglial activation and synaptic pruning in schizophrenia
